best_for: Windows users who move files to web servers, NAS boxes or S3 buckets and want a two-pane file manager, plus admins who script transfers.

points.title: Six protocols in one client
points.text: WinSCP speaks SFTP, SCP, FTP, FTPS, WebDAV and S3. You can sign in with a password, a public key, keyboard-interactive or Kerberos.

points.title: Built for scripting
points.text: Its scripting mode automates uploads and syncs, and a .NET assembly, also exposed to COM, lets PowerShell, VBScript, Python and other languages drive it. The assembly is under the Mozilla Public License 2.0.

points.title: Edit files on the server
points.text: A built-in text editor opens remote files and saves them back, which saves a download and re-upload for small changes.

points.title: Windows only
points.text: There is no Mac or Linux version; the project says it can run there through Wine. It supports Windows 7 SP1 through Windows 11 and Server 2025. WinSCP 6.3.7 was the last release for Windows XP SP2.

points.title: 32-bit by default
points.text: The main release is 32-bit and runs on 64-bit Windows; a 64-bit build is experimental. The installers listed here are x86, per user or for all users, plus an MSI. The Windows listing keeps 40 versions.

points.title: Portable takes setup
points.text: A portable build keeps settings in an INI file, but still writes a seed file and temp files on the host computer until you point those to relative paths.
